---
name: figma
description: Bring Figma into a HyperFrames video - rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion (frames read as states, not slides), shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when the person asks to use a Figma design, frame, logo or brand in a video; a bare figma.com link is not that ask.
---

**Running the CLI:** every `npx hyperframes <command>` here, the beacon included, means `node <SKILLS>/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs <command>` run in the project, where `<SKILLS>` holds this skill's folder ([rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md)).

**Usage note:** before the first one, tell the person once: "I'll send HyperFrames a usage note (linked to your account if signed in); say no to skip." Unless they say no, run `npx hyperframes events --skill=figma` once as this skill starts.

# Figma → HyperFrames

Every import happens at build time and freezes a local file with its source recorded under `.media/`, so renders never call Figma and re-running a command re-imports only what changed. Assets, tokens and components go over REST with a token; motion and shader data need a Figma connector, or a native export from the person.

## Access

`FIGMA_TOKEN` in the shell or the project `.env`. Check it exists before the first command; if not, tell the person how to make one and stop: figma.com → Settings → Security → Personal access tokens, read-only **File content** and **File metadata**, plus **Library content** for `tokens` on non-Enterprise plans. They set it themselves; never ask them to paste it into the chat.

| Error | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `BAD_TOKEN` (401) | Expired or revoked: make a new one |
| `FORBIDDEN` (403) | The message names the missing scope, or the file isn't visible to the account |
| `REQUIRES_ENTERPRISE` (403, variables) | Not a failure: the published-styles fallback already ran |
| `RATE_LIMITED` (429) | Already retried with backoff; wait a minute or import fewer nodes per call |

## Commands

- A layer, logo or image: `npx hyperframes figma asset '<url or fileKey:nodeId>' [more refs] --format svg|png --scale 2 --description "<what it is>" [--entity "<brand mark>"]`. SVG for vectors and logos, PNG at 2x for raster. Several nodes of one file in one call render in a single request; `--entity` lets `/media-use` find a brand mark later.
- Brand colours and type: `npx hyperframes figma tokens <fileKey>`. Run it before `component` and paste the printed entries into `data-composition-variables`. Without Enterprise it falls back to published styles. A connector can supply variables there instead: cache its raw response in `.media/figma-cache/` and write the bindings to `.media/figma-bindings.jsonl` (`{kind:"binding", figmaId, sourceFileKey, compositionVariableId:"figma:<name>", version}`).
- A frame as editable HTML at exact geometry: `npx hyperframes figma component '<url or fileKey:nodeId>'`, packaged under `compositions/components/<name>/`. A fill bound to an imported token comes out as `var(--slug, #literal)`, so one variable re-brands every import; an unknown token stays a literal marked `data-figma-unresolved`: import that library's tokens and re-import. Ask once which file a library is; never match by hex.
- Check hero components against Figma's pixels (`figma asset <same node> --format png`). Text drift is the usual cause; report drift you can't fix instead of hand-tweaking the import.

## Motion (connector)

Usage note (unless the person said no): these phases have no CLI touchpoint, so run `npx hyperframes events --skill=figma-motion` when you begin and `npx hyperframes events --skill=figma-motion --event=skill_completed --outcome=success|error` when done. Same for shaders (`figma-shaders`) and storyboards (`figma-storyboard`).

1. Fetch motion context for the parent frame in one recursive request; cache the raw JSON in `.media/figma-cache/`.
2. Normalise with `motionContextToDocs(raw, { selectorFor, repeat })` from `@hyperframes/core/figma`, never by transcribing keyframes. It reads the motion.dev snippets (the CSS snippets stretch durations), drops loop-wrap tail keyframes and keeps bezier eases. `selectorFor` returns the ids from the component import.
3. `motionToGsap(doc)` → `emitTimelineScript(spec)`, injected after the GSAP and CustomEase tags: paused, finite, a literal `window.__timelines` key. Named eases outside the mapped set fall back to linear; say so.
4. Verify against Figma's own export: `node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/verify-motion.mjs --reference <export.mp4> --render <render.mp4> --crop WxH+X+Y`. It compares motion between samples, so static drift cancels out, and fails under 15 dB (faithful ≈ 20+, diverging ≈ 5). Measure `--crop` from the render's card edges. A fail means fix the translation, not the threshold.
5. A track that won't translate: export it, freeze the MP4 and place it as `<video class="clip">`.

## Shaders

Figma's export path flattens shaders to their base colour, and shader source is only reachable for library-published styles. Ask the person for a native export of that frame (PNG or MP4) and place it as an asset or clip.

## Storyboards: frames are KEYFRAMES, not slides

Two frames holding the same element describe that element's state through time: animate the element between the states. Playing the frames back to back as stills is the failure mode.

1. Scenes are every frame-sized node in the section, named frames and loose full-frame rectangles alike: filter by size, not type or name. Order by `absoluteBoundingBox.x`.
2. Match children across neighbouring frames by name first, then by similar size and position. Tween geometry between states; crossfade two exports in place when the pixels changed. Export one asset per element, not one still per frame. Unmatched children enter or exit at their scene's beat.
3. Text nodes below the strip are motion notes for the scene above them, not on-screen copy. A note about motion inside a scene ("lines reveal one after another") means import that frame as a component and animate it.
4. Export in batches of about 4 scene frames per call: past about 12 ids `/v1/images` times out.
5. Frames that are one product UI in successive states: rebuild the UI as live DOM: code what changes state, freeze what doesn't, and treat each frame change as an interaction to perform (the cursor moves, clicks, the screen responds), not a tween to apply.
6. Stills are the fallback, only for frames with no shared elements.

Never leave a Figma URL in the composition.

# Running the HyperFrames CLI

`<SKILLS>` is the folder that holds the loaded skill's folder. Every skill and reference writes
the CLI as `npx hyperframes` (or bare `hyperframes`). Run each of those commands as:

```bash
node "<SKILLS>/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs" <command> <args...>
```

Run it in the user's project directory, never in the skills directory. npm starts in the home
folder, so the project's `package.json`, `node_modules` and `.npmrc` cannot choose the CLI or the
registry; the CLI then moves into the project and works there. This holds for every command,
including the usage beacon, and for a project the person received from someone else. Do not run
`npx hyperframes` in the project directly, and do not run a project's own scripts or wrappers in
its place unless the person asks for that command by name.

For bundled Node helpers, use the same launcher with
`--script <absolute-script-path> <args...>`. Helpers that call the CLI then run it through the
launcher.

## Standalone skill installs

Without a plugin manifest, the launcher runs the newest compatible published CLI. To select a
release, put `--cli-version latest` or `--cli-version <exact-version>` before the command.
Take an exact version from the person, from the version an upgrade moves the pins to, or from
`--cli-version latest --version`. Never take it from the project's own files: a `package.json`
pin does not choose the CLI unless the person asks for that release. The launcher refuses a release older than its floor (currently 0.9.80), the oldest one with
the protections for received projects, and its error names the floor.
Use the launcher from the loaded skill installation for commands shown in CLI output, too.
For example, run `node "<SKILLS>/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs" --cli-version latest --version`
to read the current release. If the installed launcher lacks this option, ask the person to update
their skills. The person installs and
updates standalone skills with `npx hyperframes skills update`.

## Plugin installs

Check the directory two levels above the loaded `SKILL.md` for `plugin.json`,
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, or
`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` identifying `hyperframes`, or a Gemini extension manifest.
That directory is `<PLUGIN_ROOT>`, and `<SKILLS>` is `<PLUGIN_ROOT>/skills`.

Call the directory you run the launcher in the working directory. It is a plugin install only
when all three of these hold:

- The name of `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` does not start with a dot, so it is not `.agents` or `.claude`.
- `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` is not the working directory, and it does not contain it.
- If `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` is inside the working directory, a folder whose name starts with a dot
  lies between them, as `.claude` does in `~/.claude/plugins/...` when you work in `~`.

Otherwise the skills are a standalone install, and the launcher ignores any manifest there.
Ignore it too, and follow the standalone rules above. The launcher refuses a manifest that
pins a release older than its floor.

For a plugin installation, these rules also apply in every skill and reference:

- Do not run `hyperframes skills update`, `skills check`, or `npx skills add`.
  The agent's plugin manager owns installation and updates. Read the skill at
  `<PLUGIN_ROOT>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; report a missing bundled skill instead
  of downloading a different release. Resolve all skill references inside this
  bundle, even if a standalone copy is also installed. Claude exposes the router
  as `/hyperframes:hyperframes`; other clients may expose `/hyperframes`.
- The launcher selects the manifest's CLI version and disables automatic standalone skill
  installation, including during `init`. The first call may download that exact
  CLI version through npm. A download failure is an error, not permission to use
  latest. Existing project dependency files and lockfiles must not be overwritten
  to match the plugin; surface a runtime incompatibility before changing them.
- For bundled Node helpers, the launcher also passes the release version to their
  dependency loader. External providers, registry downloads, and existing project
  dependencies have their own versions; a plugin version alone does not freeze those inputs.
- Treat the plugin directory as read-only. Put outputs and temporary work in the
  project or a temporary directory. Pass this plugin root and launcher convention
  to any delegated agent so it does not fall back to global skills.

Newer skills come through the client's plugin update flow and a session reload,
which the person runs. Do not update an installed plugin yourself.

The launcher suppresses CLI update notices as well as standalone skill refreshes, including when running an older CLI with a stale notice cache. It passes the release as `HYPERFRAMES_PLUGIN_VERSION` for plugin-aware helpers and as `HYPERFRAMES_SKILL_PKG_VERSION` for the existing helper-package bootstrap. Our release process versions those packages together.
